gear.desc:wood_pickaxe: Stone comes away under it as rubble. Bare hands take none. It is the least tool that breaks stone.
gear.desc:wood_axe: Bare hands take timber slowly, and this takes it faster. It is cut from planks of the first logs.
gear.desc:wood_shovel: Turf, sand and snow come away faster with it than by hand. Stone breaks under it slowly and gives nothing.
gear.desc:wood_sword: Enough for the small feeders that come up round a first camp. A great feeder cannot be killed with wood.
gear.desc:wood_bow: Its string is plant fibre. It throws the flint arrows we cut at the workbench.
gear.desc:stone_pickaxe: Knapped rubble on a haft is the second pick. With it, iron ore comes out of its rock whole.
gear.desc:stone_axe: Knapped rubble makes a heavier head than planks. A trunk comes down to it sooner.
gear.desc:stone_shovel: Gravel turned with it sometimes gives up flint, which heads the first arrows.
gear.desc:stone_sword: Anything harder than stone turns this edge. It is rubble knapped along a stick.
gear.desc:stone_bow: Rubble weights both tips. It throws the same flint arrows harder than the plank bow.
gear.desc:iron_pickaxe: Under an iron pick the gem Hīrak comes out of its rock whole. Iron ore itself comes faster than under stone.
gear.desc:iron_axe: An iron head brings oak and pine down far quicker than knapped stone.
gear.desc:iron_shovel: Clay, sand and snow move faster under beaten iron than under knapped stone.
gear.desc:iron_sword: A Nihirakka opened in a Sealed Store sometimes has iron bars in it, from the stored iron it ate.
gear.desc:iron_bow: Barbed arrows for it come off the same anvil, and Kammār sells them.
gear.desc:iron_staff: The crystal throws off an iron seat. Soft iron soaks up part of every throw. Rehakār sells a staff like this one.
gear.desc:iron_totem: On this one the small feeder is a green lump with a thorn. It takes its body from the iron billet.
gear.desc:iron_melee_0: Thorn and tooth of the common kinds turn on it. After each first kill they come harder, and it turns less.
gear.desc:iron_melee_1: In the Sealed Stores, Nihirakka stand in the shape that old plate like this had on its frames.
gear.desc:iron_melee_2: Plate is iron alone, with no hide, fibre or bone in it. The anvil shapes every piece.
gear.desc:iron_ranged_0: We rivet iron to sheep or boar hide at the brow and over the ears.
gear.desc:iron_ranged_1: The arms stay free to draw. Iron covers the chest, and hide the rest.
gear.desc:iron_ranged_2: Iron is riveted at the knee, where an archer kneels.
gear.desc:iron_magic_0: An iron band wound with Crystal Fiber. It is the first circlet a crew can make.
gear.desc:iron_magic_1: Thin iron under Crystal Fiber. Rehakār cuts lines in hearthstones and says the fibre is cut the same way.
gear.desc:iron_magic_2: Iron strips hang from the waist under Crystal Fiber. The fibre is plant fibre laid round crystal at the workbench.
gear.desc:iron_summon_0: Iron covers the face. Bone is set at the cheeks on the Line Frame.
gear.desc:iron_summon_1: Iron over the shoulders, set with bone from the pot. Harness of every metal is made on the Line Frame.
gear.desc:iron_summon_2: With mask, mantle and wraps all worn, a totem's bearer can have one more small feeder at the hand.
gear.desc:lumenite_pickaxe: Jalit ore and Black Glass both yield to a pick of the gem. An iron pick reaches neither.
gear.desc:lumenite_axe: Its edge is finer than iron's. A blow from the side splits it.
gear.desc:lumenite_shovel: It is cleaved flat on the anvil's edge, along the gem's own joints.
gear.desc:lumenite_sword: Kankāl's carcass was full of the gem. Blades like this were cleaved from it on the anvil's edge.
gear.desc:lumenite_bow: Kammār calls the gem a stone, since it takes an edge and no fire touches it.
gear.desc:lumenite_staff: Seated on the gem, the crystal loses less of a throw than on iron. Rehakār holds that Hīrak is crystal gone past use.
gear.desc:lumenite_totem: What forms on this one keeps the colour of the gem in its head.
gear.desc:lumenite_melee_0: Hīrak riveted over a cap of hide.
gear.desc:lumenite_melee_1: This cuirass takes more of the gem than any other piece. There is far less Hīrak in the rock than iron.
gear.desc:lumenite_melee_2: No low feeder can eat Hīrak. The gem has set too far.
gear.desc:lumenite_ranged_0: Dug with an iron pick, the gem at the brow came out of its rock whole.
gear.desc:lumenite_ranged_1: Hīrak is the one gem among the metals. It is cleaved and riveted to hide. No fire touches it at any step.
gear.desc:lumenite_ranged_2: Hide leggings with Hīrak at knee and shin. The gem lies nearer the floor than most iron does.
gear.desc:lumenite_magic_0: No hand can drive Hīrak, which has set past crystal. The Crystal Fiber wound on this band carries the line.
gear.desc:lumenite_magic_1: Over the gem, the fibre carries what the arm drives, as lines cut in a hearthstone do.
gear.desc:lumenite_magic_2: Hīrak strips hang from the waist under Crystal Fiber. A Recall Stone has the same gem at its middle.
gear.desc:lumenite_summon_0: Neither bone nor Hīrak goes soft under a feeder's touch. The mask is made of both.
gear.desc:lumenite_summon_1: Cleaved gem lies across the shoulders, with bone from the pot set between the plates.
gear.desc:lumenite_summon_2: Hīrak is cut from deep rock, where no born person goes.
gear.desc:cinder_pickaxe: Antar ore in the hollow yields to a Jalit pick and to nothing softer.
gear.desc:cinder_axe: A Jalit head brings a trunk down faster than a Hīrak one.
gear.desc:cinder_shovel: No fire a person lights moves Jalit ore. Maruhar's remains, ringed with Deep Rock, loosened the bar for this blade.
gear.desc:cinder_sword: The first blade that cost a great kill. Before Maruhar died, no crew had a Jalit bar. Unlike Hīrak, it does not split.
gear.desc:cinder_bow: Once she has bars to spare, Kammār sells Jalit arrows for it.
gear.desc:cinder_staff: Jalit makes a harder seat than Hīrak. The throw goes harder, and it costs the arm more.
gear.desc:cinder_totem: From a Jalit billet the small feeder takes the look of an ember in the air.
gear.desc:cinder_melee_0: Kammār can shape a bar of Jalit and cannot make one. Its ore needs great remains, and no born person gets those.
gear.desc:cinder_melee_1: Jalit plate is harder than any plate of the metals above it in the rock.
gear.desc:cinder_melee_2: To reach this ore a crew first needs a Hīrak pick, so the gem comes before the metal.
gear.desc:cinder_ranged_0: Molten rock in the deep is stone the sand kinds fed on until it ran. Jalit is iron that ran with it.
gear.desc:cinder_ranged_1: Leather of hide and Jalit. The ore was cut a few strides from molten rock.
gear.desc:cinder_ranged_2: Black Glass forms where rock ran and set, and it lies beside Jalit ore. One Hīrak pick takes both.
gear.desc:cinder_magic_0: Its band ran in Maruhar's furnace. Rehakār sells fibre of the kind wound on it.
gear.desc:cinder_magic_1: A badly laid line leaks into the arm. The fibre is laid on the Line Frame under even tension for that reason.
gear.desc:cinder_magic_2: Set at that depth and heat, Jalit sits harder than the iron above it.
gear.desc:cinder_summon_0: Fire does nothing to Jalit, which came out of the molten deep.
gear.desc:cinder_summon_1: Maruhar's remains lie in a ring of Deep Rock, which the burrower passed through and could not eat. The bar ran there.
gear.desc:cinder_summon_2: A furnace of remains is a store with no hand on it. The one that ran these bars draws feeders for as long as it stands.
gear.desc:umbrite_pickaxe: With it a crew can take Tala ore, lower in the hollow near the standing water.
gear.desc:umbrite_axe: Fungus Stem is the timber of the hollow. It falls to this head as a trunk falls to iron above.
gear.desc:umbrite_shovel: Fungal Turf lifts with it. The Hollow Rock under the turf needs a pick.
gear.desc:umbrite_sword: Harder than Jalit. It is the first blade of a metal cut inside the hollow.
gear.desc:umbrite_bow: Arrows cross a ward freely. From inside a held place, a bow reaches past its edge.
gear.desc:umbrite_staff: Lines run down the wood from grip to head. There the crystal sits on Antar, the first seat of a metal cut in the hollow.
gear.desc:umbrite_totem: Antar heads it. What forms there is dark and keeps to the air.
gear.desc:umbrite_melee_0: Antar cost the Hollow Gate first, and that frame needed Kankāl's remains.
gear.desc:umbrite_melee_1: Asikavak grow plates of this metal on their bodies. This cuirass was beaten from bars at the anvil.
gear.desc:umbrite_melee_2: Kammār sells Antar bars once Guhamāt is dead. Its carcass is full of the metal, and crews bring her more than they use.
gear.desc:umbrite_ranged_0: Its hide is from the living ground and its metal from the hollow, where no pack goes.
gear.desc:umbrite_ranged_1: Only a pick of Jalit or harder takes Antar ore.
gear.desc:umbrite_ranged_2: Antar ore ran in a Maruhar Furnace, in the same bed as Jalit.
gear.desc:umbrite_magic_0: Crystal stands in the hollow and fills its geodes. None of it there has set into gem.
gear.desc:umbrite_magic_1: No householder will live where this metal is cut. The hour there never moves on to dawn.
gear.desc:umbrite_magic_2: The strips were beaten at the anvil and hung on fibre laid at the Line Frame.
gear.desc:umbrite_summon_0: Shade Flesh comes from Tama. They took their bodies in the hollow and went up out of it, and none is left below.
gear.desc:umbrite_summon_1: Antar plates on a backing of bone, shaped on the Line Frame.
gear.desc:umbrite_summon_2: Strapped on, these wraps come through a fall with the body, as all worn gear does.
gear.desc:noctrium_pickaxe: This is the pick that opens Ākās ore, once a crew is through to the islands.
gear.desc:noctrium_axe: The hollow's lower metal, on a felling haft. Fungus Stem comes down to it faster than to Antar.
gear.desc:noctrium_shovel: Tala ore came out from near the floor of the hollow under an Antar pick.
gear.desc:noctrium_sword: Tala lay lower than Antar and set harder. An Antar edge turns on this one.
gear.desc:noctrium_bow: Jīmūt never lands, so no ward turns it, and we brought it down with arrows. Its carcass held bars of Tala.
gear.desc:noctrium_staff: A staff throws as hard as its seat is hard. This seat is Tala, harder than Antar.
gear.desc:noctrium_totem: Two carved bones flank the Tala head. The small feeder eats the flesh on them.
gear.desc:noctrium_melee_0: Kammār counts Tala a metal apart from Antar. She has seen both only as bars a crew brought her.
gear.desc:noctrium_melee_1: Tala plate over the chest. It turns more than Antar plate does.
gear.desc:noctrium_melee_2: Guhamāt hung from its cavern roof by its own growth. Its remains run this metal, in a ring of Hollow Rock.
gear.desc:noctrium_ranged_0: A Sagāl opened over the pot sometimes has Tala ore in it.
gear.desc:noctrium_ranged_1: Feeders are up at every hour in the hollow. The ore was cut among them, with no daylight to stop them coming up.
gear.desc:noctrium_ranged_2: In Guhamāt's furnace the ore runs and is never hot to the hand.
gear.desc:noctrium_magic_0: A Tala band wound with Crystal Fiber, for the brow of one who drives a staff.
gear.desc:noctrium_magic_1: Rehakār sells Crystal Fiber like that in this robe. The Tala under it is ours, from the hollow.
gear.desc:noctrium_magic_2: Laid in the same Guhamāt Furnace, Tala runs slower than Antar.
gear.desc:noctrium_summon_0: No pack or march comes into the hollow, where this ore is cut, since the stores are on the living ground.
gear.desc:noctrium_summon_1: Bone from the pot, set in Tala across the shoulders.
gear.desc:noctrium_summon_2: Worn whole, a Tala harness lets the hand have a small feeder more than Antar harness did.
gear.desc:aether_pickaxe: With this pick a crew can cut Patik ore on the islands.
gear.desc:aether_axe: Island Log comes down to it. On the islands the hour does not move.
gear.desc:aether_shovel: Island Soil and Island Turf lift with this blade. Under them is Island Rock, where the metal for it lay.
gear.desc:aether_sword: Of the living ground's metals, only Gahan is harder than this blade.
gear.desc:aether_bow: Its arms are Ākās from the islands, strung with plant fibre.
gear.desc:aether_staff: From Ākās up, a seat is hard enough that a throw is not spent on the first body it meets.
gear.desc:aether_totem: Here the small feeder forms white, and flies.
gear.desc:aether_melee_0: No bed on the islands marks anything, so a fall there ends at a bed on the living ground.
gear.desc:aether_melee_1: Jīmūt's remains are built into the frame of the Island Gate. Without that gate no crew reaches this metal.
gear.desc:aether_melee_2: Ākās greaves. The ore was cut on the islands, where the sky stands at one dusk.
gear.desc:aether_ranged_0: Ākās lies in more veins through island rock than iron does below.
gear.desc:aether_ranged_1: Tala is the softest pick that takes this ore.
gear.desc:aether_ranged_2: The Ākās on these leggings is riveted over hide from the living ground.
gear.desc:aether_magic_0: Island crystal is pale, from the lees of whatever fed there.
gear.desc:aether_magic_1: Crystal Fiber over Ākās plates. None of us knows what passes along the fibre from the arm, and Rehakār does not either.
gear.desc:aether_magic_2: Ākās lies in island rock overhead. Only a gate reaches it.
gear.desc:aether_summon_0: Ratan's body held bars of Ākās. One went into this mask.
gear.desc:aether_summon_1: Bone and Ākās across the shoulders, set on the Line Frame.
gear.desc:aether_summon_2: These bars came back from the islands through the Island Gate.
gear.desc:prism_pickaxe: Patik takes Gahan rock, which no metal of the living ground cuts.
gear.desc:prism_axe: Crystal through the metal shows along the edge of the head.
gear.desc:prism_shovel: Patik ore first runs in a Ratan Furnace, ringed with Island Rock.
gear.desc:prism_sword: Patik neither splits like crystal nor bends like iron. Crystal and metal set in it together over the islands' age.
gear.desc:prism_bow: Kuranga carried bars of this metal in its body. No Patik is cut on the living ground.
gear.desc:prism_staff: Crystal sits at the head and runs through the Patik seat behind it. The throw goes on through whatever it hits first.
gear.desc:prism_totem: A lit splinter forms on this one.
gear.desc:prism_melee_0: Sakal on the islands feed on Patik seams. Opened, they carry bits of the ore.
gear.desc:prism_melee_1: Patik ore yields to an Ākās pick and to nothing softer.
gear.desc:prism_melee_2: Only Gahan is harder than Patik, and only a Patik pick lifts Gahan.
gear.desc:prism_ranged_0: Patik and hide at the chest. Sakal had been grazing the seams where this ore was cut.
gear.desc:prism_ranged_1: Once Ratan's furnace has run the ore into bars, the anvil works it like any other.
gear.desc:prism_ranged_2: Both gates had to stand before a crew could cut this ore.
gear.desc:prism_magic_0: Crystal in the metal and Crystal Fiber over it, at the brow.
gear.desc:prism_magic_1: Ratan's furnace is ringed with Island Rock, which Ratan could not loosen where it lay.
gear.desc:prism_magic_2: Old crystal is as hard as gem. The Patik under this fibre has it all through.
gear.desc:prism_summon_0: Bone sits at the cheeks of this mask, and Patik's crystal shows across its face.
gear.desc:prism_summon_1: A Ratan Furnace draws feeders like any store with no hand on it. The bars for this mantle ran in one.
gear.desc:prism_summon_2: Patik and bone wound round the legs.
gear.desc:eclipse_pickaxe: It breaks any rock that lies over the floor. It does not mark the floor. No tool we have does.
gear.desc:eclipse_axe: With a Gahan head, a trunk comes down faster than with any other metal.
gear.desc:eclipse_shovel: A Gahan blade. Turf and sand lift fastest of all under it.
gear.desc:eclipse_sword: Gahan is violet like Chandasāvak. Some of us say that kind is made of this ore.
gear.desc:eclipse_bow: Kuranga's remains, ringed with Black Glass, run the only furnace that moves this metal.
gear.desc:eclipse_staff: Gahan is the hardest seat we have. Its throw passes through more than one body, and costs the arm the most.
gear.desc:eclipse_totem: What forms on a Gahan head runs on four legs and carries tines, as Kuranga does.
gear.desc:eclipse_melee_0: A Gahan helm. The metal is worked like iron and set far harder.
gear.desc:eclipse_melee_1: No metal we have found is harder than the Gahan in this plate. Nothing a crew wears turns more.
gear.desc:eclipse_melee_2: Kuranga answers bait only at night, since the sun undoes its kind.
gear.desc:eclipse_ranged_0: Only a Patik pick takes the ore. A crew needs both gates before it can cut the ore of its own floor.
gear.desc:eclipse_ranged_1: Hide and Gahan over the chest. The lees through the metal set long before any of us came up at the mouth.
gear.desc:eclipse_ranged_2: Gahan lies so low that the floor is the next stride down.
gear.desc:eclipse_magic_0: Lees set through the metal, and Crystal Fiber laid over it.
gear.desc:eclipse_magic_1: Gahan strips lie under the fibre, harder than the backing of any other robe.
gear.desc:eclipse_magic_2: This metal makes the Cairn Key, because nothing softer holds its charge.
gear.desc:eclipse_summon_0: A Gahan mask, set with bone at the cheeks.
gear.desc:eclipse_summon_1: Of all the carcasses, Nihān's held the most bars. Every one was Gahan.
gear.desc:eclipse_summon_2: Strips of Gahan with bone between them, bound from knee to ankle.
gear.desc:cairn_edge: Taken out of Nihān, from the store under the Cairn that it had eaten into. It reaches further than any blade we make.
gear.desc:cairn_bow: Nothing we make throws as hard. It came out of Nihān with the rest of the store it had eaten.
gear.desc:cairn_staff: Old work from the base under the Cairn, eaten by Nihān and cut out of it. Its throw goes through more than one body.
gear.desc:cairn_totem: Its head is a lamp from the Cairn's housing, cut out of Nihān with the rest of the store.
gear.desc:arrow: Grouse feather fletches a flint head. Of the five heads, flint is the softest.
gear.desc:barbed_arrow: Nihirakka leave these behind, from the stored arrows they ate. The anvil makes them too.
gear.desc:ember_arrow: A Jalit head comes off the anvil hot. It burns what it enters.
gear.desc:void_arrow: Moth Dust is on the shaft where feather would be, behind an Antar head.
gear.desc:prism_arrow: Patik makes the hardest head we have.
gear.desc:hide_0: Sheep or boar hide, cut to a cap at the workbench. It turns little.
gear.desc:hide_1: The first sheep and boar a crew brings down give the hide for this vest.
gear.desc:hide_2: Worn with the cap and vest, these trousers let a body move a little quicker.
gear.desc:cutter_saw: A cutter's two-handled steel saw. It fells timber faster than any axe made here.
mod.desc:keen: The edge closed to a single line, with no flaw anywhere along it.
mod.desc:savage: Quenched in lees, or passed once through a feeder. It loosens a little where it cuts.
mod.desc:swift: Less metal went into it than its shape suggests, and it comes round quicker.
mod.desc:heavy: Dense, with more metal in it than its size. It hits harder and swings slower.
mod.desc:dull: The bar had half set before the last blows, and the edge never closed.
mod.desc:blessed: It set all at once, in one working, with no soft place in it. The born call that favour.
mod.desc:warding: More metal set where blows land than anywhere else on the piece.
mod.desc:stalwart: It set dense throughout, so it turns more and weighs more.
mod.desc:brittle: Hammered after it had set. It has cracks too fine to see.
mod.desc:arcane: Its grain runs one way from hand to head, and a line cut along it leaks less.
mod.desc:radiant: Old lees has set into the metal, as in Gahan ore, and shows as a faint cold light.
mod.desc:menacing: A grain of a strong kill's lees is in it. Where the bearer strikes, it loosens a little.
mod.desc:vital: A body wearing it takes more harm before it gives out.
mod.desc:fleet: While it is worn, the legs carry a body a little faster.
mod.desc:lucky: Kills made by its bearer give up a little more, and more blows go in deep.
